1.title: Put battery wires into board
1.say: Hold the board steady, then push the black side wire into the left end of the top edge so it stays firm. Hold the board, then push the red side wire into the right end of the top edge so the wires stay apart.
placements: power wire joined to black battery lead for minus side (in the video: white wire) → hole at left end of far short edge of white hole board, several holes left of the other wire, pushed straight down until it grips; video does not show printed numbers so match the picture

power wire joined to red battery lead for plus side (in the video: blue wire) → hole at right end of far short edge of white hole board, a few holes right of the first wire, pushed straight down until it grips; video numbers not readable so match the picture
watch_for: if both wires are in the same row of holes the circuit cannot work, so move one a few holes away
if a wire wobbles or falls out it is not pushed deep enough, so push gently until you feel it grip
1.check_yourself: It should look like the white board sitting flat with two thin wires standing straight up from the far edge and spaced apart.

2.title: Lay striped part across board
2.say: Push one leg of the little striped part into the same row as the left wire so they join inside. Push the other leg into an empty row a few holes to the right so the part lies flat.
placements: little striped part with two thin legs 220 ohm resistor (in the video: small blue part) → left leg in same five-hole row as left power wire and right leg in empty five-hole row a few holes to the right, lying flat across top of board; video does not show printed numbers so count from left edge and match the picture
watch_for: if both legs are in the same row the part is shorted, so move one leg to a different row
if a leg shares a row with the right side wire the path is wrong, so keep it a few holes left of that wire
2.check_yourself: It should look like a tiny striped bridge lying flat across the top of the white board with its legs in two different rows.

3.title: Plug in the light
3.say: Push the shorter leg of the small light into the same row as the striped part so they join inside. Push the longer leg of the small light into the same row as the right wire so the light can glow.
placements: small light with one shorter leg and one longer leg with flat side on short side (in the video: blue LED) → shorter leg in same five-hole row as right leg of striped part and longer leg in same five-hole row as right power wire, standing straight up on right end of board; in the video: glowing blue at right edge
watch_for: if the light stays dark the legs are likely swapped, so switch them so the longer leg shares the right wire row
if both legs sit in the same row the light cannot glow, so move one leg to a different row
3.check_yourself: It should look like the small light standing straight up on the right end of the white board and glowing bright blue.
